You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

steps.output:
For ARC grids with a sparse colored motif embedded in a noisy 0/background-color field, a task may ask to find every translation where the motif's colored-cell mask lands entirely on zeros, then recolor those zero cells with the motif color. Preserve the original motif and every nonmatching cell. Match the original orientation only; do not rotate or reflect unless demos show otherwise. Ignore motif bounding-box cells that are not colored: the match condition is that all motif cells land on 0, not that the whole bounding box matches a fixed pattern. Overlapping matches should produce the union of their motif cells. Demonstrated with a 3-colored 4x5 mask: two same-orientation placements on zeros were recolored, including overlaps, and output differences exactly equaled the union. Another 6-cell 1 mask in a 0/9 field had three placements; the output was the motif color at all their cells. Previous examples also confirmed no rotated/reflected matches. Use demos to verify target background, motif color, and whether orientation changes are allowed. Practical caution: transcribing a grid with even one omitted cell can hide a valid match and produce an invalid-sized output; verify every row has the stated width before matching and before submission. Confirmed again in task-58fa3f1c: a sparse 8-cell color-5 mask in a noisy 0/9 grid had exactly two translations whose mask cells were all 0; stamp 5 on both, preserve the original motif and all other cells.

Another accepted instance (task-58fa3f1c): on a 29x11 grid with background 6, scattered zero cells, and an 8-shaped L triomino with mask offsets {(0,0),(0,1),(1,0)}, the rule was to stamp 8 over every translation whose three mask positions were all originally 0. There were 25 placements; preserve all 6s and unmatched 0s and take the union if placements overlap. This confirms the rule also applies when the nonzero background is 6 and the motif has only three colored cells. Compute matches from the original grid, not incrementally from already-stamped cells.

Additional accepted instance (task-58fa3f1c, 16x18): background 0 with scattered color-3 noise and a 7-cell color-2 stencil. In its 3x4 bounding box, the stencil mask offsets (0-indexed) are {(0,0),(0,2),(0,3),(1,1),(1,3),(2,1),(2,2)}. Search all in-bounds translations in the original input and accept one exactly when all seven mask cells are 0; bbox holes are irrelevant. There were 22 placements, with top-lefts (0,7),(0,9),(0,12),(1,3),(1,10),(1,11),(1,12),(3,1),(3,13),(4,2),(5,8),(7,5),(8,0),(8,1),(9,0),(9,1),(11,5),(12,6),(12,7),(12,8),(12,9),(13,6). Recolor the union of their mask cells to 2, preserving original stencil, color-3 noise, and unmatched zeros. Accepted first submission. Reinforces the same-orientation, original-grid mask match across another nonzero stencil color and a denser/asymmetric mask.

Accepted test (task-58fa3f1c, 13x13): background 8, zero target cells, and a 5-cell color-5 stencil with offsets {(0,0),(0,1),(0,2),(1,1),(2,1)} (a top horizontal bar with a two-cell stem below its center). Search original grid for translations whose five mask cells are all 0, ignoring other cells in the 3x3 bounding box. Four matching top-lefts were (2,1),(2,2),(2,4),(4,3). Recolor the union of those five-cell placements to 5; preserve all other cells and the original stencil. First submission accepted. This directly confirms the same-orientation mask-stamping rule for a 5-cell mask against zero speckles on background 8.

Accepted test (task-58fa3f1c, 28x13; background 9, motif color 8): The 9-cell mask offsets were {(0,0),(1,0),(1,1),(2,0),(3,0),(3,1),(4,0),(4,1),(5,0)}. Search only same-orientation translations where all mask positions are 0 in the original grid, ignoring bbox holes; recolor the union to 8. Valid top-lefts: (9,11) and (14,0). One failed submission contained a single accidental extra 8 at (15,11); ensure the row-5 endpoint of placement (9,11) is at row 14, not 15. The corrected output was accepted.


Newly verified 27x20 test (task-58fa3f1c): background 9, output/motif color 6; the source motif at rows 7-8, cols 16-19 has mask offsets {(0,0),(0,1),(1,2),(1,3)}. Valid same-orientation translations whose four mask cells are all original 0s have top-lefts (2,14),(3,15),(5,1),(6,10),(7,7),(11,15),(14,13),(15,4),(15,5),(15,6),(16,1),(18,13),(21,3),(21,11),(25,5). Recolor the 55-cell union to 6. The first submission used the correct rule but failed because input was mis-transcribed at (16,19): the true value is 9, not 0. Corrected output was accepted. Check source input values against the prompt, not only row widths; one bad copied digit can make an unchanged cell wrong even if it does not affect the match set. Five fresh demonstrations with varying sparse stencil masks/background colors further confirmed the same rule: same-orientation translations only, match on mask cells being 0, ignore bbox holes, take union of overlaps, and preserve the source stencil and all other cells.
